title: DR1 gives each review card a single Change link in its title; the frontend puts a Change link on every row, and two identically-labelled ones on the species card.

finding.frontend: Almost every summary row carries its own Change link in a third column — twenty-six of them on the captured page, on all but the five rows of the species card. They are built by src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/rows/summary-row.js:14-21, which attaches a change action to each row, and each one targets the page that collects that single answer. Several rows in the same card resolve to the same page, so the card for arrival details offers five separate links to the same port-of-entry page. On the species card the pattern breaks visibly: the card title carries two links side by side, both showing the word "Change" and distinguished only by visually hidden text ("commodity 1" and "animal identifiers for commodity 1"), so a sighted user meets "Change  Change" with nothing to choose between them.
finding.prototype: DR1 puts exactly one Change link in each card's title bar and none on any row — app/views/partials/review-summary-card.html:22-28. One card, one place to go back to. The link is dropped altogether when the card is read-only, because the same macro renders it only when the card carries a change target.
finding.difference: Move the change action from the row to the card: drop the per-row actions in summary-row.js, give each card a single change target aimed at the page that section starts on, and render it in the card title. The species card then has one link rather than two, which removes the duplicate visible label. This depends on the six-section layout — which card a Change link belongs to is decided by that regrouping — so do it in the same pass or immediately after.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding, on a Draft notification, a frontend review card whose title bar carries exactly one Change link and whose rows carry none.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs and both full-page screenshots; counted the Change links in the frontend DOM (grep -c 'summary-list__actions' = 26, grep -c 'port-of-entry?change=1' = 5); read summary-row.js and the DR1 review card partial. Rubric 2 fired on two counts: the finding said "twenty-two" row-level Change links where the page renders twenty-six, and "four separate links to the same port-of-entry page" where the arrival card renders five. Rubric 3 fired: the falsifier as written — "a card whose rows carry no Change links" — is satisfied by the species card on the very page the finding describes, and by every card on fe-check-answers-submitted, so it would have falsified a true finding. Counts and falsifier corrected; the substance stands.
finding.correction: Claimed twenty-two row-level Change links; there are twenty-six (four in Import details, four in Additional animal details, six in Arrival details, five in Transport details, six in Roles and addresses, one in Contact address; the species card's five rows carry none). Claimed four links to the port-of-entry page from the arrival card; there are five (port of entry, arrival date, means of transport, transport identification, transport document reference — the transit-countries row targets a different page). Both counts fixed in the frontend slot. The falsifiedBy as written fired against the finding's own evidence and has been replaced with the DR1 pattern it was meant to describe. DR1's one-link-per-card claim re-checked against app/views/partials/review-summary-card.html and confirmed in the dr1-review-notification DOM: eleven cards, eleven title Change links, and none of the thirty-one rows carries an action.

relatedTo.why: which page a card's single Change link targets is settled by the DR1 card grouping
